title: Network Participation Agreements: Start of the Interest Clock on Repayments of Over-recoveries
content:
When Cascade repays a primary care dentist under the Cascade DHMO Primary Care Dentist Agreement, one of the **Network Participation Agreements**, for an over-recovery, interest runs on the repayment from a clock start up to the repayment date. An over-recovery is the amount by which a dispute decision lowered an overpayment below what had already been refunded or withheld on it.

**Rule on the clock start.** The clock start of the repayment interest is set by when the decision was made and when the practice paid:

- when the decision's resolved date is after its resolution due date, the clock runs from the resolution due date;
- when the decision was made on or before its resolution due date, and the practice's latest refund on the decided overpayment is dated on or after the dispute's filing date, the clock runs from that refund date;
- in any other case, this rule does not move the clock start.

## Terms read from the records

- **The decision** is the agreement's most recent dispute decision. The rule reads its resolved date, its resolution due date, its filing date and the overpayment it decided. Where two decisions share the latest date, the one listed first on the agreement's records is taken.
- **The practice's latest refund** is the most recent refund received from the practice against the decided overpayment.
- **The repayment date** is the date of the agreement's most recent claim payment remittance.
- **Counting the clock.** Days are counted from the clock start to the repayment date: the start date is not counted and the repayment date is.

## Condition table

| Resolved after the due date? | Latest refund on the decided overpayment dated on or after the filing date? | The clock runs from |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | Either | The resolution due date |
| No | Yes | That refund date |
| No | No refund, or only refunds before the filing date | Not moved by this rule |

## Hypothetical cases

- A dispute is filed 3 April, due 3 May, and resolved 10 May. It was resolved after the due date, so the clock runs from 3 May. A repayment dated 20 June then counts 48 days.
- A dispute is filed 3 April, due 3 May, and resolved 28 April. The practice refunded the overpayment on 6 April. The clock runs from 6 April.
